arxiv-2109-13750.title: Strictly atomic modules in definable categories
arxiv-2109-13750.creator: Mike Prest
arxiv-2109-13750.description: Abstract If 𝒟 {\cal D} is a definable category then it may contain no nonzero finitely presented objects but, by a result of Makkai, there is a lim → \varinjlim -generating set of strictly 𝒟 {\cal D} -atomic modules in 𝒟 {\cal D} . These modules share some key properties with finitely presented modules.

arxiv-2207-08041.title: Personalized PCA: Decoupling Shared and Unique Features
arxiv-2207-08041.creator: Naichen Shi naichens@umich.edu
arxiv-2207-08041.description: Abstract In this paper, we tackle a significant challenge in PCA: heterogeneity. When data are collected from different sources with heterogeneous trends while still sharing some congruency, it is critical to extract shared knowledge while retaining the unique features of each source.

arxiv-2212-00168.title: Robust Circuitry-Based Scores of Structural Importance of Human Brain Areas
arxiv-2212-00168.creator: Dániel Hegedűs, Vince Grolmusz
arxiv-2212-00168.description: Abstract We consider the 1015-vertex human consensus connectome computed from the diffusion MRI data of 1064 subjects. We define seven different orders on these 1015 graph vertices, where the orders depend on parameters derived from the brain circuitry, that is, from the properties of the edges (or connections) incident to the vertices ordered.

arxiv-2306-15461.title: Distinguishing Legendrian knots in topological types 7 4 7_{4} , 9 48 9_{48} , 10 136 10_{136} with maximal Thurston–Bennequin number
arxiv-2306-15461.creator: Maxim Prasolov and Vladimir Shastin
arxiv-2306-15461.description: Abstract . In a recent work of I. Dynnikov and M. Prasolov [ 8 ] a new method of comparing Legendrian knots with nontrivial symmetry group is proposed. Using this method we confirm conjectures of [ 5 ] about Legendrian knots in topological types 7 4 7_{4} , 9 48 9_{48} and 10 136 10_{136} .

arxiv-2504-04351.title: DDPT: Diffusion-Driven Prompt Tuning for Large Language Model Code Generation
arxiv-2504-04351.creator: Jinyang Li, Sangwon Hyun, M. Ali Babar
arxiv-2504-04351.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in code generation. However, the quality of the generated code is heavily dependent on the structure and composition of the prompts used. Crafting high-quality prompts is a challenging task that requires significant knowledge and skills of prompt engineering.

pmc-11355002.title: Revision of the Genus Laelius (Hymenoptera, Chrysidoidea, Bethylidae) from China
pmc-11355002.creator: Chunhong Wang, Junhua He, Xuexin Chen
pmc-11355002.description: Simple SummaryThe cosmopolitan genus Laelius Ashmead belongs to the subfamily Epyrinae and includes 68 valid species. Members of Laelius mainly attack larvae of larder beetles (Coleoptera, Dermestidae), which are commonly known as pests of stored products. The taxonomic study of Laelius in China is far from enough, with only two species recorded.

pmc-11445187.title: Preoperative MRI-based radiomic nomogram for distinguishing solitary fibrous tumor from angiomatous meningioma: a multicenter study
pmc-11445187.creator: Mengjie Li, Shengli Fu, Jingjing Du, Xiaoyu Han, Chongfeng Duan, Yande Ren, Yaqian Qiao, Yueshan Tang
pmc-11445187.description: PurposeThis study evaluates the efficacy of radiomics-based machine learning methodologies in differentiating solitary fibrous tumor (SFT) from angiomatous meningioma (AM).Materials and methodsA retrospective analysis was conducted on 171 pathologically confirmed cases (94 SFT and 77 AM) spanning from January 2009 to September 2020 across four institutions. The study comprised a training set (n=137) and a validation set (n=34).

pmc-11621565.title: Bacterial products initiation of alpha-synuclein pathology: an in vitro study
pmc-11621565.creator: Octavian Costin Ioghen, Gisela Gaina, Ioana Lambrescu, Emilia Manole, Sevinci Pop, Teodora Maria Niculescu, Oana Mosoia, Laura Cristina Ceafalan, Bogdan Ovidiu Popescu
pmc-11621565.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Parkinson’s Disease (PD) is a prevalent and escalating neurodegenerative disorder with significant societal implications. Despite being considered a proteinopathy, in which the aggregation of α-synuclein is the main pathological change, the intricacies of PD initiation remain elusive. Recent evidence suggests a potential link between gut microbiota and PD initiation, emphasizing the need to explore the effects of microbiota-derived molecules on neuronal cells.

pmc-12444378.title: Measuring the socio-economic and environmental outcomes of regenerative agriculture across spatio-temporal scales
pmc-12444378.creator: Katherine Berthon, Ruth Wade, Pippa Chapman, Coline C. Jaworski, Jonathan R. Leake, Niamh McHugh, Lisa Collins, Tim Daniell, Yu Zhao, Penelope Watt, Bob Doherty, Peter Jackson, Lynn V. Dicks
pmc-12444378.description: Regenerative agriculture aims to produce food while simultaneously improving soil health, supporting biodiversity, reducing input costs and enhancing climate resilience. Evidence on its environmental and socio-economic impacts across different systems and climates remains limited, with few studies measuring multiple outcomes following whole farming system transition.

pmc-12539566.description: Sebocrine adenoma is an extremely rare benign primary neoplasm of the adnexal structures with complete excision usually being curative. They are not associated with significant recurrence, locally aggressive behaviour or metastasis unlike that of the sebaceous carcinoma.

pmc-12599014.title: Bayesian enrollment modeling for several emergency medicine clinical trials
pmc-12599014.creator: Jonathan Beall, Sharon D Yeatts, Robert Silbergleit, Lori Shutter, Frederick Korley, Byron Gajewski
pmc-12599014.description: BackgroundAccrual of participants into clinical trials is a fundamental and important aspect for the management of trial progress. Monitoring of trial accrual often provides insight into the potential timing of key study events, such as interim analysis, as well as the feasibility of the overall trial to enroll the projected sample size in the original estimated timeline.

pmc-13677739.title: A hypothalamic circuit links high-fat diet exposure to anxiety-like behavior and anxiety-associated hyperphagia
pmc-13677739.creator: Peng Wang, Jun Li, Xin Cheng, Wei Chen, Zhengyu Li, Zheng Fang, Dijia Wang, Bin Mei, Hu Liu, Shaohua Hu, Zhilai Yang, Jiqian Zhang, Gaolin Qiu, Xin Qing, Xuesheng Liu
pmc-13677739.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Obesity and anxiety disorders are frequently comorbid, yet the neural circuit mechanisms linking metabolic and affective states remain incompletely understood. Here, in male mice exposed to long-term high-fat diet, we identify a hypothalamic circuit comprising arcuate nucleus agouti-related protein neurons and paraventricular nucleus corticotropin-releasing hormone neurons that regulates anxiety-like behavior under metabolic stress, with downstream recruitment of lateral hypothalamic area glutamatergic neurons to modulate feeding in a state-dependent manner.
